question: In brief, what makes someone a traveller (musafir)?
answer:
I got a lot of feedback. A lot of people said, you gave a 45-minute talk, and we are not able to listen to 45 minutes. So I'm just going to give the one-minute response from last week: safar is not a distance, it is a state of mind. You are a musafir when you travel outside of your city to a distance that you, and a reasonable person as well, would consider travel. Because we don't want a crazy person who says across the street, this is safar. Somebody who is an 'aqil baligh person would say, this is travel.

What this means is that it is relative, and that you don't need to ask a faqih. If you are asking somebody, you don't understand the response. You do not come to a shaykh and say, 'Shaykh, I travel from this to this, am I musafir?' **You know when you are a musafir.**

And it is possible that two people can do the same journey, and one of them is considered a musafir and the other not, depending on their culture and habit. The one who takes a private jet every day to work 200 miles away, and he goes at 8 a.m. and comes back at 5 p.m., is not a musafir. And the one who goes the same distance for a one-day trip, and he's not a regular, and he's going... It's up to your mindset and your culture and your habit. So you know when you are a musafir. That is a two-minute response.
